hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: One same-job pair under identical registered batched Muon, 500K and 60 passes, differing only in training.weight_decay. Two physical sessions per kernel; planned pause 187488 then terminal 234360; no scientific schedule reset; 60-pass cosine unchanged; continuation submitted by the desktop owner next morning; no unattended polling service.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: NEGATIVE/NULL closes the weight-decay lever for K1 batched Muon at 500K. Single predeclared point: no second weight_decay value, no learning-rate change, no post-hoc grid, no module stacking regardless of outcome.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: NOMINATE only if both seeds give candidate-minus-control selected MAE <= -3 meV, both paired 2000-bootstrap 95% uppers < 0, both final and last-five matched-pass deltas < 0, and both kernels pass strict native/replay. NOMINATE authorizes only a separately authorized confirmatory pair against the AdamW reference; no adoption, no full-data, no automatic successor. A single seed never nominates.
hypothesis.observed_deficiency: The batched-Muon gain over AdamW at 500K shrinks with exposure (-7.93 meV at 20 passes, -4.42 at 40, -1.81 at 60). Whether stronger decoupled decay recovers late-pass development MAE under the same optimizer is unmeasured.

trajectory.question: Does raising recipe-level decoupled weight decay from 1e-5 to 0.05 reduce the selected development MAE of original K1 under batched FP32 Muon at 500K and 60 passes, reproducibly across two initializations?
